message: In the 40 metre footbridge baseline concept, the first vertical bending mode confirmation has low damping uncertainty. To check it I used simple mass estimation (the 10000 kilogram modal mass estimate (E2)). I found 1.9 hertz first mode with about 0.4 percent damping and half-sine antinode at midspan, according to Bachmann and Ammann, 1987. I propose retaining midspan as Tuned Mass Damper (TMD, mass on spring with damper tuned to bridge mode) location, thank you Vibration Control Specialist. My position: ready because baseline frequency and mode placement are confirmed. In the under-deck Tuned Mass Damper (TMD) concept, the tuning choice has 1.81 hertz versus 1.86 hertz question. To check it I used vetted Den Hartog calculation with mode layout (the Den Hartog optimum result (E3) and the under-deck layout sketch (E4)). I found 1.81 hertz damper frequency with 500 kilograms mass at 5.0 percent mass ratio, according to Den Hartog, 1934. I propose twin 250 kilogram units hidden below girders, thank you Retrofit Integration Architect. My position: ready because correct mass-ratio optimum is demonstrated. In the same retrofit concept, the crowd acceleration acceptance has comfort target concern. To check it I used response simulation (the two-degree-of-freedom response simulation (E6)). I found 0.74 metres per second squared with 9.44 percent effective damping reaching Comfort Level (CL, Setra comfort grade) CL2, according to Setra, 2006. I propose accepting the concealed twin-unit proposal. My position: ready because frequency, damping and comfort are evidenced.
